assign.now: building items 7 and 8: the ✦ dot + the mic sounds
steps: Read the brief, the existing Widget.Pulse dot, rail.js's sheet close/open, and Mic.js's beep()
The dot becomes the ✦ glyph, on by default, dimmed-not-hidden when off
Remove the level meter bars everywhere (Widget, Composer, Widget.css, docs)
The dot floats free of the sheet on a real close, back home on reopen
Prove the sounds and the dot headless, with a real fake-audio mic device

action.why: item 1: the dot is the ✦ glyph (same text the rail's own AI button uses), colored --prim, scaling with level; item 2: pulse defaults true on Widget.prototype, the level meter bars (composer_meter, .ux-dictate-widget-meter*, the `level` option everywhere) are deleted outright; item 3: Widget.Pulse gets a float(on) method that moves the real dot element (not a copy) into a shared position:fixed holder at the bottom right of the viewport; DrawerRailSheetChat.hide()/show() call it so a real close with the mic still listening leaves only the dot on screen, and reopening brings it back inline

decision.question: how the dot shows "mic is off" without the old dark "tap to talk" card
options: keep the dark overlay, just change the dot's shape
drop the overlay, dim the dot instead (never hide it) and keep an invisible tap-anywhere catcher over the feed
decision.chose: drop the overlay, dim the dot instead
decision.why: the brief is explicit: "when the mic is off, it is dimmed (low opacity) but still visible" — a second, louder off-cue (the dark card) would say the same thing twice; the invisible catcher keeps "tap anywhere in the feed starts it" working exactly as before

decision.question: how the floating dot (after the sheet closes) is built
options: a second, separate dot element that mirrors the real one's level/click state
move the SAME dot element into a shared fixed holder, and back
decision.why: law 6, one of everything — a second copy would need its own level feed and click wiring kept in sync by hand forever; moving the real node keeps its listeners and its live CSS variable for free, and `locked()` already un-floats it the instant the mic actually stops, so there is nothing extra to keep in sync when the mic is tapped off while floating
